page.layout: One column of running text, full width. No marginal notes, no footnotes, no catchword or signature. Running head at top, page number at top right.

main_text.l: standi ut occasionem cito nanciscaris,
Deum Opt. Max. & ego efflagito, &
omnes literati deprecantur; quæ aberrata
fuerunt in ἀπογράφῳ[?] Samaritano, quod
mihi misisti, quoniam ita desiderasti, lu-
bens transmitto: ista exscripta fuerunt
ex cap. 12. Deuter. à v. 27. ad finem cap.
facile autem hæc reperies, si sectiones li-
bri tui sectionibus libri mei respondeant.
Dividunt Samaritani singulos libros
Mosis in varias sectiones, quas קצין[?] vo-
cant, quæ parasc his[?] Judæis longe bre-
viores sunt; librum quintum, qui nobis
est Deuteronomium in 166. Katsin distin-
guntur, quarum 71. ab initio versus 29.
atque ab his verbis incipit אני
עקריהוה[?] initio igitur, ver. 27. ואדמה sanguinem
[?]irrepsit, dicendum enim רם[?] ut pau-
lo post, vel רמה[?] Nomen illud, ut scri-
ptum est, terram significat vel rubedi-
nem; fieri tamen potest, ut Aleph sit hæ-
manticum in eo nomine, ut aliquando
Chaldæis, in fine vers. 28. באות[?]
ponitur pro Hebræo-Samaritano בעיני[?] in oculis, suspicor scriptum esse, בהאות[?] in præ-sentia,

page.notes: Running head and page number are printed in the header; the page number reads as 198 but is doubtful, hence [?]. The Greek word ἀπογράφῳ and the Hebrew words (קצין, אני עקריהוה, רם, רמה, באות, בעיני, בהאות) are hard to read at this scan resolution and are marked [?]. The leading "N" before "irrepsit" is unclear and may be a Hebrew letter. "parascbis" is a doubtful reading of "parashis". The word "sanguinem" is italic. The right side of the scan shows the edge of the neighbouring page and show-through, which were left out.
